extracted.intended_audience: IP office analysts, policymakers, statisticians, researchers and IP professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, metrics and interpretive guidance for patent/trademark office procedural statistics (applications, grants, pendency, examiner FTE, class counts and origin/multiplier rules) used to compare offices and analyze filing trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total applications processed
rubrics_metrics.description: Total applications processed by an office (table column heading: 'Total applications processed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per office as a primary activity measure; used alongside granted/rejected/withdrawn counts to evaluate office throughput. Numbers may differ slightly from other report tables owing to different extraction dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of applications granted by an office (table column heading: 'Granted').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core output metric reflecting positive final decisions. Use with care for cross-office comparisons because offices have different practices and reporting dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of applications rejected by an office (table column heading: 'Rejected').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation caveat: 'rejection' is not recorded as a final decision in some offices (example: Canada records required applicant actions and considers inability to provide information as abandonment rather than rejection). Similar procedural differences exist in Australia. These differences complicate harmonized comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawn or abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of applications withdrawn or abandoned (table column heading: 'Withdrawn or abandoned').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures applications that did not reach a final grant or rejection. Combined with rejection counts to understand attrition, but office-specific practices affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of examiners (FTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full time equivalent number of examiners employed by the office (table column heading: 'Number of examiners (FTE)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a capacity/resource indicator. FTE allows comparison across offices with different staffing models. Consider in ratio to applications processed to assess productivity and workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: First office action (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time (in months) to first office action (table column heading: 'First office action (months)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pendency metric reflecting how quickly an office issues its initial substantive action. Useful for comparing applicant experience across offices. Values can be affected by backlog, examination procedures, and prioritization rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final office decision (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time (in months) to final office decision (table column heading: 'Final office decision (months)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures overall pendency until grant, rejection or abandonment decision. Important for assessing speed of resolution; subject to variation from differences in procedure and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application class count (trademark class count)
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of Nice classes specified in trademark applications ('the application class count' / 'class count').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class counts harmonize differences across offices that allow single- vs multi-class filings and provide a comparable measure of trademark filing activity. Offices vary in filing practices: some allow only single-class filing, others permit multi-class. Use class counts for international comparisons rather than raw application counts where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent application/grant counts by origin (multiplier for regional offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalent applications/grants by origin apply a multiplier for regional offices (example: EUIPO applications are multiplied by the number of member states to create an equivalent application count).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method makes filings at regional offices comparable to filings at national offices when reporting by applicant origin. For example, a non-resident filing at EUIPO counts as 27 applications abroad (EU member states) while an EU resident filing counts as 1 resident + 26 abroad. Caveat: equivalent-by-origin data are incomplete when some offices do not report by origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non-resident filing (office data vs origin data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of filings as resident (filed at applicant's home/regional office) or non-resident (filed at foreign offices); office data record applications received by an office, origin data record where applicants reside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to distinguish domestic market demand from cross-border filing behavior. In 2022 resident filing constituted about 83.5% of global trademark class counts and non-resident about 16.5%. Interpretation should account for regional filing options (e.g., EUIPO) and large domestic markets (e.g., China) which skew shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of class counts to improve international comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparing class counts across offices improves international comparison of filing volumes because it accounts for single- vs multi-class filing regimes and class specification differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class-count based comparisons began in 2004 for WIPO reporting. When harmonized using class counts, 2022 trademark filing decline is less pronounced but still substantial. Analysts should prefer class counts when comparing offices with different filing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of year-on-year trend changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on attributing causes for increases/decreases in filings: changes may stem from economic expansion/contraction, filing regulation changes, or normalization after atypical spikes (e.g., pandemic-related surges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attribute trend changes to a single factor without further analysis; consider resident vs non-resident composition, domestic policy/regulatory shifts, and exceptional events (e.g., COVID-19). Examples: 2022 declines may reflect return to normal after 2020 surge or local economic/regulatory factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking and concentration effects (top offices and multiplier influence)
rubrics_metrics.description: How office rankings and concentration are influenced by large domestic filing volumes and regional multipliers (e.g., China high resident filings; EUIPO multiplier effect boosting equivalent abroad counts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting top-office standings and market concentration, account for domestic filing dominance (e.g., China's large resident filings) and regional office multipliers (EUIPO). These factors can magnify the apparent activity of particular origins and offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonization caveats and data incompleteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and reporting differences between offices make full harmonization difficult; some data (e.g., equivalent by origin) are incomplete and not all offices report by origin. Notation: '..' indicates not available, 'n.a.' indicates not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise caution comparing metrics across offices. Examples: 'rejection' not recorded as final decision in Canada (treatment as abandonment), and different definitions/timings can produce discrepancies. Always consult footnotes and source notes when using WIPO statistics.
